label: Folder → Cactus Describe
info: Watches a directory for new image files. When one appears, sends it to the cactus-mirage add-on and saves the JSON result next to the image (with a .json extension).

name: Build paths
Tag the result
func:
// Stash the cactus JSON under msg.result and build a small summary for debug.
const r = msg.payload || {}
const sceneBits = r.scene
  ? Object.entries(r.scene).map(([k,v]) => `${k.replace(/_/g,' ')}: ${v}`).join(', ')
  : ''
const objList = (r.objects || []).map(o => o.name).join(', ')

msg.result = r
msg.payload = [
  `📸 ${msg.imageName}`,
  sceneBits ? `Scene: ${sceneBits}` : null,
  objList ? `Objects: ${objList}` : 'No objects detected',
  (r.text && r.text.length) ? `Text: ${r.text.map(t => '"' + t.string + '"').join(' ')}` : null,
  `Inference: ${r._ms || '?'} ms`
].filter(Boolean).join('\n')

return msg

name: Prep JSON body
Setup
info:
1. Edit the watch node's directory to your snapshot folder.
   Common HA paths: /config/snapshots/  /config/www/captures/  /media/camera/
   On Windows Node-RED: C:\\Users\\you\\Pictures\\snapshots\\

2. Make sure the directory exists and Node-RED has write access to it
   (the .json sidecar files get written there).

3. The watch node watches ALL files in the directory — the filter node
   immediately drops anything that isn't a recognized image extension.

4. The 1-second delay after the watch fires lets the camera finish writing
   the file. If you see 'Could not decode image' or partial results, increase
   to 2 or 3 seconds.

5. Each image triggers ONE describe call. The same file being modified later
   (e.g. timestamped rewrites) will trigger again — that's usually what you want.
